mainTopic: יעקב's missing fourteen years with עבר, the end of the first פרק, and the משנה and sources for reading the מגילה in order
overview: The גמרא asks why the תורה records ישמעאל's lifespan, and answers that it helps us work out יעקב's age. Adding up the years from the פסוקים makes יעקב 116 when he came to מצרים, but he told פרעה he was 130. The גמרא explains that the missing 14 years were spent learning in the house of עבר. A ברייתא shows that these years were not punished as time away from his parents: יוסף was separated from יעקב for only 22 years, which matches 20 years with לבן plus 2 years on the road home. The first פרק then ends with its הדרן. The new פרק opens with a משנה listing how the מגילה must be read: in order, from a written scroll, and in an understood language or in אשורית, from a scroll written in אשורית on parchment with ink. The גמרא finds the source for reading in order in 'נזכרים ונעשים' and extends the rule to הלל, קריאת שמע and תפלה, with four אמוראים giving sources for הלל. It then begins to find the source for שמע through a dispute between רבי and חכמים, and the פסוק behind רבי's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the תורה list ישמעאל's years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה bothers to record ישמעאל's lifespan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why were the years of ישמעאל counted in the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question: why tell us how old ישמעאל was? This question sets up the whole calculation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישמעאל is not a righteous figure, so recording his age seems unnecessary. The גמרא assumes every detail in the תורה has a purpose and goes looking for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Ishmael, son of אברהם and הגר

phrases.english: Why were the years of Ishmael counted?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of recording ישמעאל's lifespan in the תורה.

steps.title: To calculate יעקב's years
steps.stepSummary: ישמעאל's lifespan of 137 years is a tool for working out יעקב's age.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written so that we can use it to calculate יעקב's years. The verse says: 'These are the years of ישמעאל's life: 137 years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ישמעאל's age serves as a measuring stick for figuring out יעקב's age. It quotes the verse saying ישמעאל lived 137 years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number 137 will be the anchor for the coming calculation. The goal is to pin down how old יעקב was at key moments in his life.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְיַחֵס בָּהֶן שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב.
phrases.english: In order to calculate through them the years of Jacob.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישמעאל's 137 years serve to calculate יעקב's age.

steps.title: ישמעאל was fourteen years older than יצחק
steps.stepSummary: Two verses show that ישמעאל was born when אברהם was 86 and יצחק when he was 100, a gap of 14 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much older was ישמעאל than יצחק? Fourteen years. The verse says אברם was 86 when הגר bore ישמעאל, and another verse says אברהם was 100 when יצחק was born.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the calculation by finding the age gap between ישמעאל and יצחק. It asks the question and answers it at once with two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Subtracting 86 from 100 gives 14 years. This is the first link in a chain that will connect ישמעאל's age to יעקב's.

Fourteen years,

steps.title: ישמעאל was 74 when יעקב was born, so he lived 63 more years
steps.stepSummary: יצחק was 60 when יעקב was born, which made ישמעאל 74 then. Since ישמעאל lived to 137, he had 63 years left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says יצחק was 60 when the twins were born. So how old was ישמעאל when יעקב was born? 74. How many years did he have left? 63.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds יצחק's age at יעקב's birth to the 14-year gap and finds that ישמעאל was 74 at that time. It then subtracts from 137 to get 63 remaining years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 60 plus 14 equals 74, and 137 minus 74 equals 63. So ישמעאל died when יעקב was 63, which is the key number for the rest of the sugya.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וְיִצְחָק בֶּן שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה בְּלֶדֶת אוֹתָם״,
phrases.english: And it is written: 'And Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them,'

phrases.aramaic: בַּר כַּמָּה הֲוָה יִשְׁמָעֵאל כִּדְאִתְיְלִיד יַעֲקֹב?
phrases.english: How old was Ishmael when Jacob was born?
Seventy-four years old.
How many of his years remained? Sixty-three.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר כַּמָּה הֲוָה יִשְׁמָעֵאל כִּדְאִתְיְלִיד יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 14-year gap to fix ישמעאל's age at יעקב's birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישמעאל had 63 years left after יעקב was born, so יעקב was 63 when ישמעאל died.

steps.title: A ברייתא: יעקב was 63 when blessed, the same time ישמעאל died
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that יעקב received his ברכה at age 63, the same time ישמעאל died. It cites the verse about עשו going to ישמעאל right after the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: יעקב אבינו was 63 when his father blessed him, and ישמעאל died at that same time. As the verse says: 'עשו saw that יצחק had blessed... and עשו went to ישמעאל and took מחלת, the daughter of ישמעאל, the sister of נביות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that links the 63 years to a specific event: the ברכה יעקב received from יצחק. It quotes the verse showing that the ברכה and ישמעאל's death happened around the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know which moment in יעקב's life matched ישמעאל's death: the ברכה, right before he ran away from home. The verse puts the ברכה and עשו's visit to ישמעאל side by side, and the next step will show that ישמעאל died at that point.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the 63-year figure and ties it to the ברכה.
steps.raayaObject: That יעקב was 63 at the time of the ברכה, when ישמעאל died.

steps.title: Why the verse mentions 'sister of נביות'
steps.stepSummary: The extra words 'sister of נביות' show that ישמעאל died after arranging the match, so her brother had to marry her off.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the verse says 'daughter of ישמעאל,' don't I already know she was the sister of נביות? This teaches that ישמעאל betrothed her to עשו and then died, and her brother נביות married her off.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the verse proves ישמעאל died at that time. The seemingly extra phrase 'sister of נביות' shows that her brother, not her father, gave her in marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ישמעאל were alive, the verse would not need to mention her brother. Naming נביות signals that ישמעאל died between the betrothal and the wedding, right when יעקב got the ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This דרשה is what actually pins ישמעאל's death to the time of the ברכה. That fixes יעקב's age at 63 when he left home.

phrases.english: From the fact that it says 'daughter of Ishmael,'

steps.raayaObject: That ישמעאל died at the time of the ברכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The seemingly extra words 'אחות נביות' in the verse.

steps.title: Adding up יעקב's age until he came to מצרים: 116
steps.stepSummary: 63 plus 14 (until יוסף was born) is 77. Add 30 (יוסף's age before פרעה) to get 107, then 7 years of plenty and 2 of famine to get 116.
steps.simpleTranslation: 63 plus 14 until יוסף was born makes 77. The verse says יוסף was 30 when he stood before פרעה, so that makes 107. Add 7 years of plenty and 2 of famine, and that makes 116.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues adding years to find how old יעקב should have been when he arrived in מצרים. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 14 years are the years יעקב worked for לבן before יוסף was born. Then יוסף was 30 before פרעה, and יעקב came down in the second year of the famine. All together this gives 116.
steps.confusionAlert: The 14 years here are not the same 14 years as the gap between ישמעאל and יצחק. These are the 14 years יעקב worked for לבן before יוסף was born.

phrases.english: Sixty-three and fourteen
until Joseph was born,
that makes seventy-seven.
And it is written: 'And Joseph was thirty years old
when he stood before Pharaoh,'
that makes a hundred and seven.
Seven of plenty and two of famine:
that makes a hundred and sixteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁתִּין וּתְלָת וְאַרְבֵּיסַר עַד דְּמִתְיְלִיד יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the confirmed 63 as a base and continues the count forward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By this count, יעקב should have been 116 when he came down to מצרים.

steps.title: But יעקב told פרעה he was 130
steps.stepSummary: יעקב tells פרעה he is 130, but the count gives only 116. Fourteen years are missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the verse says: 'פרעה said to יעקב, How many are the days of the years of your life? And יעקב said to פרעה, The days of the years of my sojournings are 130 years.' Yet by our count, he was only 116.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction: the calculation gives 116, but יעקב himself said 130. The next step explains where the missing 14 years went.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every number came from a verse, so the gap cannot be a simple math mistake. Somewhere in יעקב's life there are 14 years the count did not include. The גמרא will go on to explain where they went.

They are, it comes out to

steps.whatToRemember: By the count of verses, יעקב was 116 when he came to מצרים, but he said he was 130. There are 14 years unaccounted for.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And Pharaoh said to Jacob,
How many are the days of the years of your life?
And Jacob said to Pharaoh,

phrases.aramaic: יְמֵי שְׁנֵי מְגוּרַי שְׁלֹשִׁים וּמְאַת שָׁנָה״,
phrases.english: The days of the years of my sojournings are a hundred and thirty years.'
But it comes out to only a hundred and sixteen!

steps.kashyaTarget: The calculation that יעקב was 116 when he arrived in מצרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יעקב explicitly says he was 130, which leaves 14 years missing from the count.

steps.title: The missing fourteen years were spent in the house of עבר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the 14-year gap: the count left out the 14 years יעקב spent in the house of עבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the fourteen years יעקב was in the house of עבר are not counted here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8. The 14 missing years were years יעקב spent in the house of עבר, and the earlier count simply did not include them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 counted as if יעקב went straight to לבן right after getting the ברכה at 63. Here the גמרא says there was a 14-year stop first, at the house of עבר. Adding those 14 years brings 116 up to 130, which matches the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; conclude from here
The house (study hall) of עבר, שם's great-grandson
He (the verse/count) does not count them

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שְׁנִין דַּהֲוָה בְּבֵית עֵבֶר
phrases.english: that the fourteen years that he was in the house of Eber
he did not count them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 14-year gap raised in Step 8.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: יעקב went straight from his father's house to לבן at age 63.
steps.terutzMaskana: יעקב first spent 14 years in the house of עבר, and these were left out of the earlier count.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms יעקב was in עבר's house for fourteen years
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that יעקב hid in the house of עבר for 14 years, and arrived at the well in ארם נהרים at age 77.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: יעקב was hidden in the house of עבר for fourteen years. עבר died two years after יעקב went down to ארם נהרים. יעקב left there and went to ארם נהרים. So when he stood at the well, he was seventy-seven years old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the answer in Step 9. The ברייתא says outright that יעקב was hiding with עבר for 14 years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 63 (the ברכה) plus 14 (with עבר) equals 77, the age יעקב was when he reached the well. The detail about עבר dying 2 years later shows that the dates of עבר's life fit this timeline. With 77 as the new starting point, the count reaches exactly 130.

keyTerms.meaning: The well where יעקב met רחל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two numbers. 77 is יעקב's age when he arrived at the well, not his age when יוסף was born. יוסף was born 14 years later, when יעקב was 91. Then 91 + 30 + 9 = 130.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a Baraita: Jacob was in the house of Eber

Eber died after went down

phrases.english: Jacob our father to Aram-naharaim, by two years,

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא מִשָּׁם וּבָא לוֹ לַאֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם,
phrases.english: he left there and went to Aram-naharaim,
it turns out that when he stood at the well

steps.raayaObject: That יעקב spent 14 years in the house of עבר before going to לבן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא giving the 14 years and the age of 77 at the well.

steps.title: How do we know יעקב was not punished for those years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that יעקב was not punished for the 14 years he spent away from his parents learning with עבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he was not punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and sets up the next proof. The question is whether יעקב was punished for being away from his parents during the 14 years with עבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being away from one's parents means missing out on כיבוד אב ואם. יוסף's 22 years away from יעקב are understood as a punishment matching יעקב's own time away. The question is whether the years of learning תורה with עבר count toward that punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he was not punished?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 14 years with עבר and asks how they affected his punishment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the 14 years with עבר were not punished as time away from his parents.

steps.title: יוסף was away twenty-two years, just like יעקב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says יוסף was separated from his father for 22 years, matching the time יעקב was separated from his own father.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: It turns out that יוסף was away from his father for twenty-two years, just as יעקב our father was away from his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. It says יוסף's 22 years away from יעקב matched יעקב's time away from יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats יוסף's separation as a matching punishment, measure for measure. So the number of years יעקב is punished for must be exactly 22. The next step uses this number to work out which years did not count.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a Baraita: It turns out that Joseph
was away from his father for twenty-two years,
just as Jacob our father was away from his father,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by citing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יעקב's punishment, matched by יוסף's separation, lasted only 22 years.

steps.title: Thirty-six years minus fourteen leaves twenty-two
steps.stepSummary: יעקב was actually away for 36 years. The ברייתא counts only 22, so the 14 years with עבר must not have been counted against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But יעקב was away for thirty-six years! Rather, the fourteen years he spent in the house of עבר are not counted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math to finish the proof. יעקב's total time away was 36 years, but he was punished for only 22, so the 14 years with עבר did not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 14 (עבר) + 20 (לבן) + 2 (the journey home) = 36. Since the punishment was only 22 years, the 14 years spent learning תורה with עבר were not held against him. That answers the question of Step 11.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source that time spent learning תורה is not punished as neglect of כיבוד אב ואם.

phrases.english: But for Jacob it was thirty-six years!
Rather, the fourteen that he was in the house of Eber
are not counted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 22 years from Step 12 to show that the 14 years were not counted.
steps.raayaObject: That יעקב was not punished for the 14 years with עבר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The gap between his actual 36 years away and the 22 years in the ברייתא.

steps.title: But יעקב was only with לבן for twenty years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: יעקב was in לבן's house for only 20 years, so why is he faulted for 22?
steps.simpleTranslation: Ultimately, the time in the house of לבן was only twenty years!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the number 22. The פסוק says יעקב was with לבן for 20 years, so where do the other 2 years come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking out the 14 years with עבר should leave only the 20 years with לבן. But the ברייתא says 22. That leaves 2 years unexplained.

phrases.english: Ultimately, those of the house of Laban
were twenty years!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף דְּבֵית לָבָן עֶשְׂרִין שְׁנִין הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 22-year figure after the 14 years were removed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 22 years of punishment in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without the 14 years with עבר, only the 20 years with לבן are left, not 22.

steps.title: He delayed two years on the road home
steps.stepSummary: The extra 2 years come from time יעקב spent on the way back from לבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because he delayed on the road for two years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. יעקב lingered for 2 years on his trip home, and those years count against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 20 years with לבן plus 2 years on the road equals 22. Unlike the time with עבר, these 2 years were not spent learning תורה, so they are counted.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because he delayed
on the road two years,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional time period: 2 years on the journey home
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the 20 years with לבן count, so the punishment should be 20 years.
steps.terutzMaskana: 20 years with לבן plus 2 years delayed on the road equals 22.

steps.title: Eighteen months in סוכות and six in בית אל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא spells out the 2 years: 18 months in סוכות, learned from the פסוק, and 6 months in בית אל, where he brought offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: He left ארם נהרים and came to סוכות and stayed there eighteen months, as it says, "And יעקב traveled to סוכות and built himself a house, and for his cattle he made booths." And in בית אל he stayed six months and brought offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the 2-year delay with a ברייתא. It shows how long יעקב stayed in each place on his way home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions booths, a house, and booths again. That is read as summer, winter, and summer, which adds up to 18 months. Add 6 months in בית אל and the total is exactly 2 years.
steps.confusionAlert: Here סכות is a place name. It has nothing to do with the holiday of סוכות.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a Baraita: He left Aram-naharaim
and came to Sukkot,
and spent eighteen months there,
as it is stated: "And Jacob traveled to Sukkot
and built himself a house
and for his cattle he made booths,"
phrases.notes: Booths for the summer, a house for the winter, then booths again for the next summer: that adds up to 18 months.

phrases.english: and in Beth El he spent six months,
and brought offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָצָא מֵאֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם וּבָא לוֹ לְסֻכּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the 2-year delay from Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That יעקב spent 2 years on the road home.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא and the פסוק in בראשית 33:17.
steps.whatToRemember: The full count is 14 years with עבר (not punished), 20 with לבן, and 2 on the road. That makes 36 years away, but only 22 were punished, matching יוסף's 22 years. All the numbers now fit, including יעקב being 130 before פרעה.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter מגילה נקראת
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the first פרק of מסכת מגילה, מגילה נקראת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter "מגילה נקראת."
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said at the end of a פרק. It closes the chapter מגילה נקראת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the chapter is finished and expresses the wish to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Megillah is read," the chapter name

phrases.english: We will return to you, "The Megillah Is Read"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the timeline sugya is resolved.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of מגילה is complete.

steps.title: The מגילה must be read in order, from a scroll, in an understood language
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a משנה. Reading the מגילה out of order, by heart, or in a translation one does not understand does not fulfill the obligation. A foreign-language speaker may hear it in his own language, or in the original אשורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone reads the מגילה out of order, he has not fulfilled his obligation. If he read it by heart, or read it in translation in any language, he has not fulfilled his obligation. But for people who speak a foreign language, we may read it to them in that foreign language. And a foreign-language speaker who heard it in אשורית (the original Hebrew) has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins. The משנה lists ways of reading the מגילה that do not count, and two cases of reading in another language that do count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three requirements here. The reading must follow the order of the text, it must come from a written scroll and not from memory, and it must be in a language the listener understands. The one exception to the language rule is the original אשורית: hearing the original text works even for someone who does not understand Hebrew.

keyTerms.meaning: Out of order; reading a later part before an earlier part
By heart, from memory, without a written text
A speaker of a foreign (non-Hebrew) language / that foreign language
The original Hebrew language and script of the מגילה
He has not fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as 'translation never works.' The first ruling (לא יצא) is about a translation the listener does not understand. Reading in a foreign language to people who speak that language does count.

phrases.aramaic: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה לְמַפְרֵעַ — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: One who reads the Megillah out of order has not fulfilled his obligation.
If he read it by heart,

phrases.aramaic: קְרָאָהּ תַּרְגּוּם בְּכׇל לָשׁוֹן — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: or read it in translation, in any language, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: Here that means a language the listener doesn't understand.

phrases.english: But for foreign-language speakers, we may read it in that foreign language,
and a foreign-language speaker who heard it in Ashurit (Hebrew) has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה לְמַפְרֵעַ לֹא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 17 closed the first פרק. This step opens the new פרק, הקורא למפרע, with its משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading out of order, by heart, or in a translation one does not understand does not count. Reading in the listener's own language, or in the original אשורית, does count.

steps.title: Pauses and dozing are fine; reading while writing or correcting needs intent
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. Reading with pauses, or while dozing, still counts. Someone who reads the words while writing, explaining, or correcting a מגילה is יוצא only if he intended to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he read it in intervals, or while dozing, he has fulfilled his obligation. If he was writing it, explaining it, or correcting it: if he intended to fulfill his obligation, he has fulfilled it, and if not, he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists situations that might seem to ruin the reading but do not. It then adds a case where the result depends on the reader's intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Interruptions and a half-awake state do not cancel the reading. When the words are read as part of another activity (writing, explaining, proofreading), the reading counts only if the person had in mind to do the מצוה. This is the idea of כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: In intervals; with breaks between parts of the reading
He directed his heart; he had intent to fulfill the מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic מקור for the discussion of whether מצוות require כוונה.

phrases.english: If he read it in intervals, or while dozing, he has fulfilled his obligation.
If he was writing it, expounding it, or correcting it,
if he directed his heart (had intent), he has fulfilled his obligation,
and if not, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of reading rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaks and dozing do not ruin the reading. Reading done while writing, expounding, or correcting counts only with כוונה.

steps.title: The scroll must be in אשורית, on parchment, with ink
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with the rules for the physical scroll. A מגילה written with various dyes or chemicals instead of ink, or on paper or untanned hide instead of parchment, is invalid. It must be written in אשורית, on a ספר (parchment), with דיו (ink).
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was written with paint, with red dye, with gum, or with vitriol, or on paper or on untanned hide, he has not fulfilled his obligation. He fulfills it only when the מגילה is written in אשורית, on parchment, and with ink.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from how the מגילה is read to what the scroll itself must be made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things can disqualify the scroll: the writing material (anything other than real ink) and the writing surface (anything other than proper parchment). The closing clause states the positive standard: אשורית script, parchment, and ink.

keyTerms.meaning: Types of paint or dye; סיקרא is a red pigment
Vitriol, a chemical used to blacken leather
Hide that was processed but never fully tanned

steps.whatToRemember: A valid מגילה is read in order, from a written text, in an understood language or in אשורית. The scroll must be written in אשורית on parchment with ink.

phrases.english: If it was written with sam or with red dye,
or with gum, or with vitriol,

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַנְּיָיר וְעַל הַדִּפְתְּרָא — לֹא יָצָא,
phrases.english: or on paper, or on untanned hide, he has not fulfilled his obligation,
unless it is written in Ashurit,
on parchment, and with ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה by moving from reading rules to rules about the scroll itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגילה is valid only if it is written in אשורית, on parchment, with ink.

steps.title: What is the source for reading in order?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of the משנה's first rule, that reading out of order does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these words derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the first rule of the משנה (reading למפרע). This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a source, not an attack. The גמרא accepts the rule and wants to know which פסוק it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (derived)? A standard request for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא, asking for the source of the rule against reading למפרע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that reading the מגילה out of order does not count.

steps.title: רבא: like the days of פורים, the reading must be in order
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the פסוק 'ככתבם וכזמנם' (אסתר ט:כז). The פסוק puts 'their writing' next to 'their times.' The days of פורים always come in order, so the reading of the text must also be in order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says 'according to their writing and according to their times.' Just as their times cannot be out of order, so too their writing cannot be out of order.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. He compares the reading of the מגילה to the dates of פורים, which can never come out of order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links כתבם (the written text) with זמנם (the dates of פורים). The 14th of אדר can never come after the 15th, and that fixed order carries over to the reading. The text must be read from start to finish in sequence.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their writing and according to their times (אסתר ט:כז)
Just as ... so too; the form of a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's first proof compares the reading to the fixed order of the days of פורים through 'ככתבם וכזמנם'. The next step challenges this source, and Step 24 replaces it.

phrases.english: Rava said: Because the verse says:
"According to their writing and according to their times."
Just as their times cannot be out of order,
so too their writing may not be out of order.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא דְּאָמַר קְרָא כִּכְתָבָם וְכִזְמַנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ככתבם וכזמנם' compares the writing to the dates. The dates cannot be out of order, so the reading cannot either.

steps.title: The verse speaks about observing, not reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's proof. The פסוק 'ככתבם וכזמנם' is about observing the days of פורים, not about reading the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is 'reading' written here at all? It is 'observing' that is written, as it says: 'That they should observe these two days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's proof. It points out that the פסוק he used never mentions reading at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full פסוק says 'להיות עושים את שני הימים ככתבם וכזמנם.' The words 'ככתבם וכזמנם' describe how to observe (עשייה) the days, not how to read the מגילה. So the comparison between writing and times cannot teach us anything about reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anything? Is it at all? (a challenging opener)
Observing or doing (celebrating the days of פורים)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not reject the rule itself. Everyone agrees reading out of order does not count. The only question is which פסוק is the right source.

phrases.english: Is 'reading' written here at all?
It is 'observing' that is written,
phrases.notes: The verse describes celebrating the days, not reading.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'That they should observe these two days.'
phrases.notes: This is אסתר ט:כז, the start of the same verse רבא quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's derivation from step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of 'ככתבם וכזמנם' as the source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse speaks of observing (עשייה), not reading (קריאה), so it cannot teach a rule about reading.

steps.title: Remembering is linked to observing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a better source: 'נזכרים ונעשים.' Remembering (reading) is placed next to observing. Observing cannot be out of order, so reading cannot be either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes from here, as it is written: 'And these days are remembered and observed.' Remembering is compared to observing. Just as observing may not be out of order, so too remembering may not be out of order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the rejected proof with a new פסוק that links reading to observing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'נזכרים' means remembering, which is done by reading the מגילה. The פסוק puts it right next to 'נעשים' (observing). From the earlier פסוק we already know observing must follow the order of the days. Through this link (היקש), reading also gets the rule of 'not out of order.'

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here (a new source replaces the old one)
It is compared (a היקש, a link drawn between two things in the same פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The final source for not reading the מגילה out of order is 'נזכרים ונעשים.' Reading (זכירה) is linked to observing (עשייה), and observing must follow the order of the days.
steps.whyThisMatters: The original פסוק is still used, but only for observing. The new פסוק carries that rule over to reading.

phrases.english: Rather, it is from here, as it is written:
'And these days are remembered and observed,'
Remembering is compared to observing:
Just as observing may not be out of order,
so too remembering may not be out of order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by providing a new source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ככתבם וכזמנם' directly teaches the order of reading
steps.terutzMaskana: 'נזכרים ונעשים' links reading to observing, and observing has to follow the order of the days

steps.title: The same rule applies to הלל, שמע, and תפלה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the rule against reading out of order also applies to הלל, קריאת שמע, and תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And the same is true for הלל, and the same for קריאת שמע and for תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that extends the 'no out of order' rule beyond the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying these texts out of order does not fulfill the obligation, just like the מגילה. This sets up the next question: where do we learn this for each one?

keyTerms.meaning: The praise chapters of תהלים (113–118) said on holidays

phrases.english: It was taught: And the same is true for Hallel,
and the same for the recitation of Shema and for prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule just derived for the מגילה to other texts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל, קריאת שמע, and תפלה must also be said in order to fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: What is the source for הלל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that הלל may not be said out of order.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this for הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule for הלל. It is setting up a list of answers that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מגילה rule came from a פסוק in אסתר, so it does not automatically cover הלל. The גמרא wants a separate source for הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: From where do we derive this for Hallel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא's ruling about הלל
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק teaching that הלל must be said in order

steps.title: רבה: From sunrise to sunset
steps.stepSummary: רבה learns it from 'ממזרח שמש עד מבואו.' The sun's path cannot be reversed, so הלל must also go in order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: As it is written, 'From the rising of the sun to its setting.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the first answer, a פסוק from inside הלל itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sun always rises in the east and sets in the west, never the other way. The פסוק ties praising ה' to that fixed order, so the praise of הלל must also follow its fixed order.

keyTerms.meaning: From the rising of the sun (תהלים קיג:ג)

phrases.english: Rabba said: As it is written:
'From the rising of the sun to its setting.'
phrases.notes: תהלים קיג:ג, a verse in הלל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fixed path of the sun from rising to setting teaches that הלל must be in order.

steps.title: רב יוסף: This is the day God made
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף learns it from 'זה היום עשה ה'.' A day follows a fixed order, so הלל must too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: 'This is the day that ה' has made.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a different פסוק from הלל as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A day has a set order: morning, then afternoon, then evening. Just as the day cannot be rearranged, הלל must be said in its proper order.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the day God made (תהלים קיח:כד)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
'This is the day that the Lord has made.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative source to רבה's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fixed order of a day teaches that הלל must be in order.

steps.title: רב אויא: Let God's name be blessed
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא learns it from 'יהי שם ה' מבורך.' The word 'יהי' (let it be) teaches that the praise must be said the way it is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא said: 'Let the name of ה' be blessed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא gives a third possible source from הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יהי' teaches that the blessing must 'be' exactly as written, which means in its written order.

keyTerms.meaning: Let God's name be blessed (תהלים קיג:ב)

phrases.english: Rav Avya said:
'Let the name of the Lord be blessed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'יהי' teaches that the praise must be said exactly as written.

steps.title: From now and forever
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק (some say רב אחא בר יעקב) learns it from 'מעתה ועד עולם.' Time only moves forward, so הלל must also go in order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק, and some say רב אחא בר יעקב, said: From here: 'From now and forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth אמורא offers the end of the same פסוק as the source. With this, the list of answers ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From now and forever' describes time, which always moves forward and never backward. So too, הלל must be said from beginning to end. This comes from the second half of רב אויא's פסוק, which focuses on time instead of the word 'יהי.'

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (marks a doubt about who said it)

steps.whatToRemember: All four אמוראים agree that הלל must be said in order. They only disagree about which פסוק in הלל teaches it: the sun's path, the order of a day, 'יהי,' or the forward flow of time.

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov, said:
From here: 'From now and forever.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth alternative source, from the end of the פסוק רב אויא used
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Time moves only forward, teaching that הלל must be in order.

steps.title: Next item on the list: the שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves from הלל to קריאת שמע and asks where we learn that שמע said out of order is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The recital of the שמע: from where do we know that saying it out of order does not count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving to the next item on its list. Just as it found a source for הלל, it now looks for a source showing that קריאת שמע said out of order does not count. This line sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words 'קריאת שמע' are shorthand. They carry over the earlier question, 'from where do we know that if one said it out of order (למפרע) he did not fulfill his obligation?', and apply it to שמע. The answer will be built from a ברייתא and a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily recital of the שמע paragraphs
Out of order (the topic being carried over from the earlier question)

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'קריאת שמע' here are not a full sentence. They are a short label that repeats the earlier question about order, now applied to שמע.

phrases.english: The recital of the Shema:
phrases.notes: Short for: 'From where do we know that קריאת שמע said out of order is invalid?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the sources for הלל, moves to the next item in the ברייתא of Step 25, קריאת שמע, and asks the same question about order.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that saying קריאת שמע out of order does not fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: The ברייתא: must the שמע be in Hebrew or any language
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי requires שמע to be said as written, while חכמים allow any language.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: The שמע must be recited as it is written. These are the words of רבי. But חכמים say: it may be recited in any language.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with an argument about saying שמע. רבי says it must be said 'as it is written', meaning in the original לשון הקודש. חכמים say any language is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first this ברייתא seems to be about language, not order. The גמרא brings it because the פסוק each side uses will become the source for the order rule. The side that does not use the פסוק for language will use it to teach that שמע must be said in order.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
As it is written (in its original language)
The words of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא has wandered off topic. The argument about language is a stepping stone. The פסוק behind it will be used to teach the rule about order.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
The Shema must be recited as it is written,
these are the words of Rabbi;
but the Sages say: in any language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that will lead to the source for the question in Step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: שמע must be said in its written language. חכמים: it may be said in any language.

steps.title: What is רבי's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי's source that שמע must be said in its original language, and begins quoting a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי? The verse states:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי requires שמע to be in its original language. It starts to answer with 'the verse states', and the actual פסוק comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking for רבי's reason sets up the key פסוק. Once we see which word רבי uses for the language rule, we will see that חכמים use that same word for the order rule. So this question is the bridge back to the main topic.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?
The verse states:
phrases.notes: The פסוק itself continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural basis of רבי's opinion in the ברייתא from Step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that רבי uses to require שמע in its original language. The answer will lead to the source for saying שמע in order.
